newsitem.title: USA: Laser Vision sees more profitability.
newsitem.headline: Laser Vision sees more profitability.

text.p: Laser Vision Centers Inc said Monday it expects more of its centers to generate profits in the coming year.

"We are excited and optimistic for the coming year as we expect continued increases in our case volume and more of our centers to achieve profitability," said John Klobnak, Laser Vision chairman, in a statement.

Laser Vision operates 40 excimer lasers in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Sweden, Finland and Greece. An excimer laser allows eye surgeons to correct nearsightedness with an outpatient procedure.
A company spokesman said that some of the company's U.S. centers are profitable and declined further comment.

Laser Vision reported a loss for its fiscal second quarter ended October 31, 1996 of $2.1 million or $0.25 a share on 8.5 million shares outstanding. This compares with a net loss of $1.5 million or $0.30 a share on 4.8 million shares outstanding in the same quarter last year.
Depreciation and amortization, non-cash items, accounted for 49 percent of the loss for the quarter.
Fiscal second quarter revenues rose to $1.9 million from $960,000 for the same period a year ago.
Laser Vision also reported that its fiscal second quarter revenues rose 28 percent from the first to the second quarter of the current fiscal year, while the net loss fell seven percent.

Laser Vision said U.S. case volume for the quarter increased by more than 40 percent over the previous quarter. Beginning in March, Laser Vision said it will begin announcing same laser sales on a monthly basis.
Shares of Laser Vision were trading off 1/8 to 5-7/8.
